easy.explanation: The Lord tells Ezekiel to prophesy against Pharaoh king of Egypt.
easy.q: To whom was the prophecy directed?

easy.explanation: Pharaoh is called “the great dragon” lying in the midst of his rivers.

answers: They would be brought out and cast away
easy.explanation: The Lord would bring them out of the rivers and leave them in the wilderness.
easy.q: What would happen to Pharaoh and the fish of his rivers?

medium.explanation: The fish clinging to the dragon picture those connected with Pharaoh’s power.
medium.q: What do the fish of the rivers represent in the passage?

answers: To emphasize his dependence on the wilderness
To emphasize his connection with the Nile and royal power
To describe his work in Tyrus
medium.explanation: The image connects Pharaoh with the rivers of Egypt and his royal claim over them.
medium.q: Why is Pharaoh described as a dragon lying in the rivers?

answers: There would be no gathering or burial
They would not enter the river
They would not fear the sword
medium.explanation: Pharaoh and the fish would be left scattered and unburied.
medium.q: In verse 5, what does “thou shalt not be brought together, nor gathered” mean?

answers: “My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself”
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh claims the river as his own and boasts that he made it himself.

answers: Their humiliation and abandonment without burial
challenge.explanation: They are cast away and left exposed to the beasts and birds.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by giving Pharaoh and the fish to the beasts and birds for food?

answers: The inhabitants of Egypt would know that the Lord is God
Pharaoh would become stronger among the nations
Israel would trust Egypt even more
challenge.explanation: The judgment would cause Egypt’s inhabitants to know that the Lord is God.
challenge.q: What result of the judgment is stated in the passage?

paragraphs.title: Egypt as a Broken Reed of Support

easy.explanation: Egypt was a staff of reed to the house of Israel.
The passage says that Egypt was a staff of reed to the house of Israel.
When Israel leaned upon Egypt, the reed broke.
easy.q: What happened when Israel leaned upon Egypt?

answers: It was a weak and unreliable support for Israel
medium.explanation: Egypt failed as a dependable support for the house of Israel.
medium.q: Why was Egypt punished according to this passage?

answers: They were wounded and made to stumble
medium.explanation: The broken reed wounded their shoulders and made their loins unsteady.
medium.q: What happened to Israel when they leaned upon Egypt?

answers: Something people rely upon for support
A place where the dead are buried
medium.explanation: A staff is something used for support, but this staff was only a weak reed.
medium.q: What does “staff of reed” mean in this context?

answers: It was based on an everlasting covenant
challenge.explanation: The reed appeared to offer support but broke when people depended on it.
challenge.q: What does the image of the reed teach about the security Egypt offered?

answers: It shows that Egypt could no longer serve as a dependable support
It proves that Egypt would rule Israel
It describes Egypt’s return to Pathros
challenge.explanation: The broken reed represents Egypt’s failure as a supporting power.
challenge.q: How is the breaking of the reed related to Egypt’s judgment?

answers: Israel relied on Egypt, but that reliance brought harm
Egypt relied on Israel and won
The two kingdoms had no connection
challenge.explanation: Israel looked to Egypt for support, but Egypt’s failure wounded and weakened them.
challenge.q: What relationship between Egypt and Israel appears in the passage?

answers: An army from Israel to defend it
easy.explanation: The Lord said that He would bring a sword upon Egypt.
The land and cities of Egypt would be desolate forty years.
easy.q: How long would Egypt be desolate?

answers: Among the nations and through the countries
easy.explanation: The Lord would scatter them among the nations and through the countries.
easy.q: Where would the Egyptians be scattered?

answers: The scattered Egyptians would be gathered and returned to Pathros
Egypt would disappear from the earth forever
Egypt would rule all the nations
medium.explanation: At the end of forty years, the Lord would gather the Egyptians and bring them back to Pathros.
medium.q: What would happen to Egypt after forty years?

answers: It would be a base kingdom
It would be the strongest kingdom
It would again be a secure support for Israel
medium.explanation: Egypt would return, but it would remain “a base kingdom.”
medium.q: What would Egypt’s status be after its return?

medium.explanation: Desolate describes a land that is ruined, deserted, and empty.
medium.q: What does “desolate” mean in these verses?

answers: It shows the breaking apart of the nation and its land
It shows the strengthening of the kingdom
It prevents the sword from coming
challenge.explanation: The judgment includes both the devastation of the land and the scattering of its people.
challenge.q: How is the scattering of Egypt’s inhabitants related to its destruction?

answers: The return does not restore its former power
The return makes Egypt ruler of the nations
The return cancels the forty years of desolation
challenge.explanation: Egypt returns, but it remains the basest of the kingdoms and cannot rule as before.
challenge.q: What limits the significance of Egypt’s return to Pathros?

answers: Egypt would no longer rule the nations or be Israel’s confidence
challenge.explanation: Egypt would be humbled so that it could no longer rule or serve as Israel’s confidence.
challenge.q: What additional purpose of Egypt’s judgment is mentioned?

easy.explanation: Nebuchadrezzar and his army served a great service against Tyrus.
easy.q: Who performed hard service in the siege against Tyrus?

easy.explanation: The army received no wages from Tyrus for the service it had performed.
easy.q: What did Nebuchadrezzar’s army not receive from Tyrus?

easy.explanation: The Lord promised to give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.
easy.q: What would the Lord give to Nebuchadrezzar?

answers: As wages and compensation for his army’s labor
So that he could restore Egypt to Pharaoh
So that he could build Tyrus
medium.explanation: Egypt would be the wages for the labor of Nebuchadrezzar’s army.
medium.q: Why was Egypt given to Nebuchadrezzar?

answers: Take its multitude, spoil, and prey
Gather Egypt’s captives without taking spoil
medium.explanation: He would take Egypt’s multitude, spoil, and prey.
medium.q: What would Nebuchadrezzar do in the land of Egypt?

medium.explanation: Spoil is property taken after conquest or victory.
medium.q: What does “spoil” mean in this passage?

answers: As a worker receiving wages for his labor
As one who depended upon Egypt
challenge.explanation: The Lord presents Egypt as wages for the work performed by Nebuchadrezzar’s army.
challenge.q: How is Nebuchadrezzar presented in this passage?

answers: Egypt serves as compensation for the labor that brought no reward at Tyrus
Tyrus receives Egypt as a gift
challenge.explanation: The land of Egypt is given as payment for the service performed against Tyrus.
challenge.q: What is the connection between receiving no wages from Tyrus and receiving Egypt?

answers: The gift was directly connected to the army’s work
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Egypt was given in return for the labor of Nebuchadrezzar’s army.
challenge.q: What does “his labour wherewith he served against it” emphasize?

paragraphs.title: A Horn for Israel and Speech for Ezekiel

easy.explanation: The Lord said, “In that day will I cause the horn of the house of Israel to bud forth.”
easy.q: For whom would the Lord cause a horn to bud?

easy.explanation: The Lord promised to give Ezekiel the opening of the mouth among Israel.
easy.q: What would the Lord give Ezekiel?

answers: That Egypt was a secure support
easy.explanation: Israel would know that the Lord is God.

medium.explanation: A budding horn symbolizes renewed strength and advancement.
medium.q: What does the budding horn symbolize for Israel?

answers: Its fulfillment would enable him to speak among the people
He would stop prophesying against Egypt
medium.explanation: The opening of his mouth points to his restored ability to speak among Israel.
medium.q: How is the opening of Ezekiel’s mouth related to his prophecy?

answers: The ability and opportunity to speak
The entrance gate of a city
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Ezekiel would be enabled to speak.
medium.q: What does “the opening of the mouth” mean?

answers: Egypt’s humiliation is accompanied by Israel’s strengthening
Egypt’s strengthening causes Israel to weaken
There is no connection between the events
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from Egypt’s judgment to the strengthening of Israel.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between Egypt’s fall and Israel’s budding horn?

answers: Recognize the prophet and know that the Lord fulfills His word
challenge.explanation: The fulfillment would confirm Ezekiel’s prophetic message and the Lord’s faithfulness.
challenge.q: What would the fulfillment of the prophecy enable Israel to do?

answers: It moves from judgment on Egypt to hope and recognition for Israel
It moves from Egypt’s salvation to Israel’s destruction
It moves from Israel’s victory to dependence on Egypt
challenge.explanation: The verse turns from Egypt’s judgment to Israel’s renewed strength and Ezekiel’s voice.
challenge.q: What change of thought appears in the final verse?
